context.audience: Northwind's VP Engineering and the two product-team engineering managers
context.decision: Approve a sixteen-week pilot of the AI-DLC across two product teams

cover.title: A governed AI-DLC for Northwind's product teams
cover.subtitle: An AI Development Life Cycle (AI-DLC) from Jira story to reviewed pull request in four months, with a person approving every decision and a report card for every story.
cover.notes: Open with the outcome: two product teams shipping stories through a governed agentic lifecycle, measured from day one.

slides.subtitle: Built from Northwind's codebase outward, proven on real stories before anything is handed over

slides.title: Agents work between gates; a named person opens each

steps.title: Requirements
bullets: Reads the Jira story
Asks when context is missing
Writes requirements

steps.title: Design
bullets: Design against your standards
Cites the pages it used

steps.title: Build
bullets: Code and tests on a branch
Every tool call guarded

steps.title: Verify
bullets: Unit, contract, performance checks
Fixes its own failures

steps.title: Review
bullets: Reviewer agent writes findings
Report card on the pull request

slides.callout: "Looks good" is not an approval. A gate opens only on an explicit approve from its named person.
slides.notes: Walk one story left to right. Stress that gates are enforced by the harness, not by convention: until the named person approves, the guard blocks the next stage's writes.

slides.title: Four agents, each with a defined job and limits
slides.subtitle: Each agent reads a schema-checked input and writes a defined output; nothing else

items.name: Requirements agent
items.in: Jira story, linked Confluence pages, Knowledge Fabric
items.limits: Writes only to the stories folder and the Jira comment it was asked for

items.name: Developer agent
items.out: Code and unit tests on a feature branch
items.limits: Only the repositories in the approved plan; never reads .env or key stores

items.name: Test agent
items.out: Unit, contract and performance tests with results
items.limits: Runs in the dev environment only; no production data

items.name: Reviewer agent
items.limits: Read-only on source; cannot merge or push

slides.notes: Limits are enforced by the policy guard, which the next slide shows.

slides.title: What happens on every tool call
slides.subtitle: Hard controls checked cheapest first; the first failure blocks the call
checks: Protected path? (.env, key stores, agent config)
Secret or personal data in the content?
Command or host outside the allow-list?

blocked.title: Blocked
blocked.text: Reason returned to the agent and written to the audit chain. No retry around the block.

pass: After the tool: redact secrets, flag injected instructions, count tokens
slides.notes: Every one of these is tested by a red-team suite of 53 cases before each release.

slides.title: What sits around the agents
slides.subtitle: Five layers; the dashed boxes are what we add to Northwind's estate
slides.notes: The harness layer is the product. Everything else is Northwind's existing estate.

slides.title: Governance, safety and observability are built in
slides.subtitle: Enforced by the framework rather than by prompt wording

items.title: Governance
bullets: People approve scope, design and merge
Agents cannot edit their own policy or config
Every decision hash-chained in the audit log

items.title: Safety
bullets: Secrets and personal data redacted before the model sees them
Prompt-injection phrases in fetched content flagged
Only allow-listed hosts reachable

items.title: Observability
bullets: Tokens, time and gates per stage
Five AI-DLC measures on every run
Guard blocks and asks counted and explained

slides.notes: Each bullet maps to a control we demonstrate in week 2.
